- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or bullish sentiment; model tends to overshoot in upward momentum phases.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged bearish sentiment or low sentiment periods; model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Lag in reaction to sentiment shifts: model often reacts to sentiment changes 1–2 days too late, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows and fails to smoothly revert to historical mean unless sentiment strongly supports trend.
- Overshoot after strong bullish sentiment spikes: model forecasts peak prices too high, then undercorrects in subsequent days.
- Underweight sentiment in early forecast windows: sentiment history is often ignored or discounted in initial 5–7 day forecasts.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish, model tends to overforecast; when sentiment is mildly bearish, underforecast.
- Correct for “sentiment lag” by adjusting forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment has recently turned negative or weak.
- Avoid overfitting to recent price trends; sentiment should override short-term momentum if it contradicts historical volatility patterns.
